working_title: Testing the Periodic-Table Hypothesis of Human Language: Predictive Evidence Favors Non-Circular Structure
alternate_title: Beyond the Periodic Table: Stress-Testing the Geometry of Cross-Linguistic Structural Space
promotion_target: formal Paper 002 after independent ARIS secondary review
core_question: Does an explicitly circular/periodic geometry provide reproducible out-of-sample organization of cross-linguistic structural relations beyond non-periodic alternatives?

stage0.claim: non-random structure exists; no periodicity inference

stage1b.claim: direct angular optimization removes obvious circular-strawman objection; global circle remains feature-count sensitive

stage1e.claim: all TLI models weaken under large geographic blocks

stage1g.claim_limit: not universal; contradicted by WALS geography transfer

current_interpretation: The tested simple global circular form of the language periodic-table hypothesis is not supported. Hierarchical/non-circular models are stronger family-held-out predictive benchmarks across TLI, GBI, and WALS, but the evidence does not establish one universal tree geometry. Geographic portability is representation-dependent and secondary.
